- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow for lingering momentum.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and true outcome shows strong mean reversion, model often underestimates volatility — increase forecast variance or add a small upward bias.  
- For 30-day horizons, model consistently underestimates early spikes (first 5–7 days) — apply a 5–10% upward bias to initial forecast values if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (0.00) and true outcome shows persistent upward movement, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to start rising 1–2 days earlier than observed.
